Values are total-population-weighted averages of county estimates [county median (interquartile range)]. Each county's published estimate is weighted by its total population; for measures defined on adults, or age-adjusted, this approximates but is not identical to a pooled value for the stratum, and the density value is the density experienced by the average resident, not total population divided by total area. Medians describe the distribution across counties. Missing counts are for all counties.

Unit of observation is the county. These are characteristics of county residents, not of patients imaged at accredited facilities; the study used no patient-level data, and cardiovascular disease prevalence, disease severity, and gender identity were not available.

Sources: CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index 2022 component estimates (American Community Survey 2018-2022) for age, race and ethnicity, poverty, insurance, and disability; County Health Rankings & Roadmaps 2024 for sex (Census population estimates) and for diabetes, obesity, smoking, physical inactivity (model-based estimates), premature age-adjusted mortality, and primary care physicians; American Community Survey 2019-2023 population with SVI land area for density. Race and ethnicity categories are mutually exclusive; all categories other than Hispanic or Latino are non-Hispanic.

County Health Rankings 2024 reports Connecticut by its former counties, so the 9 Connecticut planning regions lack those measures; other missing values are as published (up to 166 counties for one measure).

Rurality strata follow the 2023 USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes. CCT = cardiac computed tomography; CI = confidence interval; CMR = cardiac magnetic resonance; EDI = economic deprivation index; IRR = incidence rate ratio; NB2 = negative binomial (quadratic variance); NE = not estimable; RUCC = Rural-Urban Continuum Code; SDI = Social Deprivation Index; SVI = Social Vulnerability Index.
